buyer_question: We plan to use python-slugify for URL slugs in a CMS we will support for years — do the install variants, the Python support matrix, the status/coverage badges and the README usage examples (unicode transliteration, max_length, stopwords, CLI) still hold on a current interpreter?

claims.text: The package can be installed from PyPI with `pip install python-slugify`, after which `from slugify import slugify` succeeds (the default install pulls in text-unidecode).
claims.source_quote:
# How to install

    pip install python-slugify
claims.probe_hint: python3 -m venv /tmp/v && /tmp/v/bin/pip install python-slugify && /tmp/v/bin/python -c 'from slugify import slugify; import text_unidecode; print("ok")'

claims.text: The alternative extra `pip install python-slugify[unidecode]` installs the Unidecode package alongside python-slugify.
claims.probe_hint: python3 -m venv /tmp/v2 && /tmp/v2/bin/pip install 'python-slugify[unidecode]' && /tmp/v2/bin/python -c 'import unidecode, slugify; print("ok")'

claims.text: With python-slugify installed, `slugify("This is a test ---")` returns 'this-is-a-test'.
claims.source_quote:
txt = "This is a test ---"
r = slugify(txt)
self.assertEqual(r, "this-is-a-test")
claims.probe_hint: python3 -c "from slugify import slugify; assert slugify('This is a test ---') == 'this-is-a-test', slugify('This is a test ---')"

claims.text: With python-slugify installed (default text-unidecode backend), `slugify('影師嗎')` returns 'ying-shi-ma', and `slugify('影師嗎', allow_unicode=True)` returns '影師嗎'.
claims.source_quote:
txt = '影師嗎'
r = slugify(txt)
self.assertEqual(r, "ying-shi-ma")

txt = '影師嗎'
r = slugify(txt, allow_unicode=True)
self.assertEqual(r, "影師嗎")
claims.probe_hint: python3 -c "from slugify import slugify; assert slugify('影師嗎') == 'ying-shi-ma', slugify('影師嗎'); assert slugify('影師嗎', allow_unicode=True) == '影師嗎'"

claims.text: With python-slugify installed, `slugify("C'est déjà l'été.")` returns 'c-est-deja-l-ete' and `slugify('Компьютер')` returns 'kompiuter'.
claims.source_quote:
txt = 'C\'est déjà l\'été.'
r = slugify(txt)
self.assertEqual(r, "c-est-deja-l-ete")

txt = 'Nín hǎo. Wǒ shì zhōng guó rén'
r = slugify(txt)
self.assertEqual(r, "nin-hao-wo-shi-zhong-guo-ren")

txt = 'Компьютер'
r = slugify(txt)
self.assertEqual(r, "kompiuter")
claims.probe_hint: python3 -c "from slugify import slugify; assert slugify(\"C'est déjà l'été.\") == 'c-est-deja-l-ete'; assert slugify('Компьютер') == 'kompiuter', slugify('Компьютер')"

claims.text: With python-slugify installed, for txt = 'jaja---lol-méméméoo--a': `slugify(txt, max_length=9)` returns 'jaja-lol'; `slugify(txt, max_length=15, word_boundary=True)` returns 'jaja-lol-a'; `slugify(txt, max_length=20, word_boundary=True, separator=".")` returns 'jaja.lol.mememeoo.a'.
claims.source_quote:
txt = 'jaja---lol-méméméoo--a'
r = slugify(txt, max_length=9)
self.assertEqual(r, "jaja-lol")

txt = 'jaja---lol-méméméoo--a'
r = slugify(txt, max_length=15, word_boundary=True)
self.assertEqual(r, "jaja-lol-a")

txt = 'jaja---lol-méméméoo--a'
r = slugify(txt, max_length=20, word_boundary=True, separator=".")
self.assertEqual(r, "jaja.lol.mememeoo.a")
claims.probe_hint: python3 -c "from slugify import slugify; t='jaja---lol-méméméoo--a'; assert slugify(t, max_length=9)=='jaja-lol'; assert slugify(t, max_length=15, word_boundary=True)=='jaja-lol-a'; assert slugify(t, max_length=20, word_boundary=True, separator='.')=='jaja.lol.mememeoo.a'"

claims.text: With python-slugify installed, `slugify('the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog', stopwords=['the'])` returns 'quick-brown-fox-jumps-over-lazy-dog' and `slugify('10 | 20 %', replacements=[['|', 'or'], ['%', 'percent']])` returns '10-or-20-percent'.
claims.source_quote:
txt = 'the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog'
r = slugify(txt, stopwords=['the'])
self.assertEqual(r, 'quick-brown-fox-jumps-over-lazy-dog')
claims.probe_hint: python3 -c "from slugify import slugify; assert slugify('the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog', stopwords=['the'])=='quick-brown-fox-jumps-over-lazy-dog'; assert slugify('10 | 20 %', replacements=[['|','or'],['%','percent']])=='10-or-20-percent'"

claims.text: Installing python-slugify also installs a command-line tool named `slugify`: `echo "Taking input from STDIN" | slugify --stdin` prints 'taking-input-from-stdin' and `slugify taking input from the command line` prints 'taking-input-from-the-command-line'.
claims.source_quote:
```
$ echo "Taking input from STDIN" | slugify --stdin
taking-input-from-stdin
```

```
$ slugify taking input from the command line
taking-input-from-the-command-line
```
claims.probe_hint: /tmp/v/bin/pip install python-slugify >/dev/null && test "$(echo 'Taking input from STDIN' | /tmp/v/bin/slugify --stdin)" = 'taking-input-from-stdin' && test "$(/tmp/v/bin/slugify taking input from the command line)" = 'taking-input-from-the-command-line' && echo OK
